label: Shallow NN
conclusions: Model explained: Shallow NN (test PR-AUC 0.689, validation 0.748; rank 1 of 1 on test PR-AUC among the saved models).

Permutation importance (test): the three features whose shuffling hurts PR-AUC most are quali_pos (0.071), grid_clean (0.064), team_best_grid (0.031). 9 of 29 features are reliably used (mean drop above 2 standard deviations); the rest could be shuffled without a detectable loss.
The validation and test rankings disagree (Spearman 0.01 over the top-10 union, 6 of the top 10 shared).

By feature group, shuffling 'grid' costs the most PR-AUC (0.178); in descending order: grid (0.178), standings (0.080), qualifying (0.072), context (0.011), constructor_form (0.011), driver_form (0.010), circuit_history (-0.006).

SHAP (test rows): the largest mean |SHAP| belong to grid_clean (0.059, 11% of the total), quali_pos (0.059, 11% of the total), team_best_grid (0.048, 9% of the total). By group the largest is 'grid' (29% of total group SHAP).

Permutation importance and SHAP disagree on the ranking (Spearman 0.36 over the top-10 union, 5 of the top 10 shared); a feature ranked much higher by SHAP than by permutation is one the model pushes on without that push improving test accuracy much.
The SHAP ranking is robust to the reference data (lowest pairwise Spearman across three references: 0.86; robust at 0.85 or above).

Across three retrained network seeds (and the saved model) the permutation rankings have pairwise Spearman between 0.43 and 1.00 over the top-10 union, and share at least 6 of their top 10 features: a network explanation is not stable across seeds.

Local: SHAP and LIME share on average 3.5 of their top-5 features across the four cases, agree in sign on 90% of LIME's top-10 features, LIME's local R2 averages 0.33 and its top-5 set is 53% stable across seeds (Jaccard).
None of these results are causal effects: a feature is important here only in the sense that this fitted model's scores depend on it.
